book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 7 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte

title: Starting beekeeping: steps and tools
competency: List the steps to start beekeeping and name beekeeping equipment.

keywords.def: A place where beehives are kept.
A tool that makes smoke to calm the bees.
A net hat that protects the face and neck from stings.
A machine that spins honey out of the combs.

en.text: To start beekeeping: establish a site, get honeybee colonies, get basic equipment and tools, and clear and fence the apiary. Productive beekeeping depends on good management and a suitable area; good site selection saves time, energy and money.

screens.title: Getting started
screens.ask: What do you need first to start beekeeping?
opts: A good site for the hives
screens.after: Beekeeping starts with a good site, then bees, tools and a fence.

screens.title: 3.5.1 Important steps to start beekeeping
table: 3. Get basic equipment, materials and tools

screens.title: 1) Site selection
paras: Productive beekeeping depends on good management and a suitable area.
Good areas must be found and checked.
Good site selection saves time, energy and money.
Hives can be traditional (hung in trees) or modern (wooden boxes).

screens.title: Key words
defs: A place where beehives are kept.

screens.text: What does good site selection save?

screens.why: These are the book's four steps.
screens.clue: Where will the bees live first?

screens.text: Chala bought bees before finding any place to keep them. Which step did he skip?
screens.why: Step 1 is the site. Bees need a suitable area before they arrive.

en.text: Besides the hive, beekeepers need equipment. Protective clothing and a veil prevent most stings. A smoker calms the bees. Table 3.2 lists veil, clothing, smoker, sprayer, hive tool, queen excluder, honey extractor, honey presser, wax extractor, honey sieve and uncapping fork.

screens.title: Dressed for bees
screens.ask: Why does a beekeeper wear a veil and a suit?

screens.title: 3.5.2 Beekeeping equipment and tools
paras: Beekeeping equipment is used in beekeeping and honey production.
You need protection from bee stings.
A smoker gives some control over the bees.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A tool that makes smoke to calm the bees.
A net hat that protects the face and neck from stings.
A machine that spins honey out of the combs.

opts: Gives some control over the bees
screens.ans: Gives some control over the bees

screens.text: Tap the beekeeping tools from Table 3.2.
screens.why: Rake is a garden tool; milk bucket is for dairy.
screens.clue: Which are for bees and honey?
Think of protection, calming and honey.

screens.text: Hiwot gets stung on the face when opening a hive. What two things would help most?
opts: A honey sieve and a bucket
screens.why: A veil protects her face, and smoke calms the bees before she opens the hive.
screens.clue: Protect the face; calm the bees.

items.text: List beekeeping equipment and tools. Tap the ones in the book.
items.why: These are in Table 3.2. Spade and sickle are garden tools.

opts: A place where beehives are kept
test.ans: A place where beehives are kept

test.text: Protective clothing prevents most bee stings.
Which is step 2 to start beekeeping?

notes.text: 3.5.1 and 3.5.2 are merged in one lesson.
The book says a hive tool "allows the beekeeper to climb up to the hives" and a smoker minimizes "biting"; a hive tool is a small lever and bees sting. Not used in graded items.
Table 3.2 gives only names and photos; the uses in the match item are added.
Activity 18 (how honey is made) is not covered by the book; left out.
